basis: Intellectual disability and limb malformations define syndrome; reflux and external auditory canal atresia are very frequent (80-99%), affecting GI and ear function.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by vertebral and metaphyseal abnormalities, scoliosis and coxa vara; no established extraskeletal organ damage.
Lipoic acid biosynthesis disorder with hyperglycinemia and progressive spastic neurologic disease; optic atrophy and visual impairment occur in 30-79%.
Malignant pancreatic tumour umbrella, predominantly exocrine; endocrine subtypes and metastatic sites do not characterize most patients across the group.
Muscular dystrophy with defining intellectual disability, present in 5/5 patients; cardiomyopathy and respiratory complications are occasional, below 30%.
Disseminated Sporothrix infection commonly produces persistent cutaneous nodules and ulcers (>30%); bone, lung and CNS involvement vary and are not reliably above threshold.
Polycystic developmental disease of the parotid salivary glands; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defining intestinal hypoperistalsis/microcolon and megacystis affect bowel and urinary tract; hydroureter and hydronephrosis support urinary dysfunction.
Benign melanocytic skin nevus composed of large epithelioid melanocytes.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with global and speech delay in 13/13; constipation (4/13) alone does not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.
Predominantly uterine/placental or gonadal trophoblastic cancer, outside the axes; frequent lung spread among metastatic cases does not establish involvement in >=30% overall.
Persistent nasal dysfunction from turbinate reduction or removal; the nose and nasal airway belong to the pulmonary axis.
Sickling hemoglobinopathy directly affects red cells and spleen; stroke, acute chest syndrome and osteonecrosis are separately diagnosed complications.
Umbrella for developmental malformations of the brain and spinal cord; extrasystem abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Molecular subtype of medulloblastoma, a primary central nervous system malignancy.
Axonal neuropathy with defining optic atrophy (10/10); muscle wasting and vocal cord paresis reflect denervation, without established intrinsic muscle or airway disease.
Congenital malformation of atrioventricular connections; associated septal and valvular defects are cardiac. Respiratory insufficiency does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
WHIM is defined by immunodeficiency, myelokathexis/neutropenia and persistent HPV warts; recurrent respiratory infections alone do not establish chronic lung damage.
Psychiatric/psychosexual disorder umbrella without defining damage to any of the 13 organ axes.
Complex I metabolic disease with basal ganglia necrosis (3/3) and regression (4/4); weakness may be central, and direct skeletal myopathy is not established.
ZFTA fusion-positive ependymoma arises in the supratentorial central nervous system.
Defining ectodermal dysplasia, ectrodactyly and macular dystrophy; dental malformations occur in 80-99%, with tooth agenesis and microdontia in 30-79%.
Intellectual disability and marfanoid skeletal abnormalities define syndrome; atrial septal defects occur in 30-79%. Palatal shape and dental crowding alone do not establish GI damage.
Type A dystroglycanopathy is defined by congenital muscular dystrophy with brain and eye anomalies; reported findings include lissencephaly and retinal degeneration.
Persistent neuropathic pain from sensory nerve injury after herpes zoster; a postinfectious sequela rather than ongoing infection.
